title: Diagnostic: Forgetting mutating
hints: Inside a non-`mutating` struct method, `self` is immutable.
Remove the `mutating` keyword from the method that changes `score`.
jsBridge: Struct methods can't modify `self` unless marked `mutating`, because `self` is an immutable copy inside ordinary methods. JS methods can always mutate `this`. The keyword makes mutation visible in the API.

compass.q: In JS, any method can change `this`. What does Swift's `mutating` annotation tell a caller that JS never does?
What does `mutating` do under the hood: is `self` passed `inout`?
Classes don't need `mutating`. Why not, and what does that say about reference types?
Protocol requirements can be `mutating`. Why must a protocol for both structs and classes declare it?
